filesystem.description: File operations — read, write, search, move files in allowed directories.

sqlite.description: Direct SQL access to JRVS memory database — query conversations, documents, chunks.

github.description: GitHub — search repos, read files, manage issues and PRs, view commits.

sequential-thinking.description: Structured step-by-step reasoning for complex multi-part problems.

brave-search.description: Web search via Brave. Set BRAVE_API_KEY in .env (https://brave.com/search/api/)

puppeteer.description: Browser automation — runs headless (no visible window). Screenshots, evaluate JS, fill forms.

slack.description: Slack — read channels, post messages, search workspace. See _setup_instructions.

mp4-downloader.description: Video downloader — search the web for videos and download them from any URL (YouTube, Reddit, tube sites, galleries). Use for any 'download/save/grab/rip that video' request. Files are saved on the downloader host, not locally.

mp4-downloader.status: READY — tested end to end (search, inspect, real download, library listing)
how_it_works: Thin MCP wrapper over the mp4-downloader web UI's HTTP API (~/mp4-downloader/webui.py).
The web UI must be running: systemctl --user status mp4-webui.service
Downloads land in ~/mp4-downloader/downloads ON THE DOWNLOADER HOST and appear in its web UI.
MP4DL_URL is the tailnet address; the server falls back to http://127.0.0.1:8766 automatically.
usage_notes: Ambiguous request? Call inspect_request first — it says whether the text is a link (download) or a question (search).
search_videos returns candidates only and downloads nothing. Show them, let the user pick, then call download_video.
Downloads outliving wait_seconds is normal — status stays 'running' and a job_id comes back. Poll check_job; never restart the download.
search_videos needs Ollama up, since the search plan is built by the local model.
